title: Evaluating and Promoting Resilience in Adolescents With Tourette Syndrome
official: Adapting and Pilot Testing Promoting Resilience in Stress Management (PRISM) for Adolescents With Tourette Syndrome and Persistent Tic Disorders: A Mixed-Methods Feasibility Study and Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: This study adapts and tests PRISM (Promoting Resilience in Stress Management), a short skills-based program that teaches resilience, for teens ages 12-18 with Tourette syndrome or persistent tic disorder. The study has three parts. First, a small group of teens and their caregivers try PRISM and give feedback to adapt it for teens with tics. Second, 15 teens complete the adapted program to see whether it is practical and acceptable. Third, 60 teens are randomly assigned to PRISM plus usual care or usual care alone, to see whether a larger trial is feasible and to get early information on resilience and other outcomes.
conditions: Persistent (Chronic) Motor or Vocal Tic Disorder
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 12-18 years
* Physician-confirmed diagnosis of Tourette syndrome or persistent (chronic) motor or vocal tic disorder per DSM-5-TR criteria
* YGTSS Total Tic Severity ≥15 (Tourette syndrome) or Total Motor/Total Phonic score ≥10 (persistent motor or vocal tic disorder)
* YGTSS Impairment ≥20
* English fluency in reading and speaking, even as a second language
* Able to understand and complete study procedures and measures

Exclusion Criteria:

* An active diagnosis of functional neurological disorder
* Beginning any new therapy within 8 weeks of study initiation
